- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) or shows strong reversal (e.g., -0.33) — add 3–5% buffer to avoid undershoot.
- Model tends to overreact to recent highs; apply mean reversion bias: if 3 consecutive forecast days exceed true outcome by >3%, adjust downward by 1–2% per day.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.4–0.7), forecast should be closer to historical 18-day moving average — use it as anchor for correction.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) — reduce first 5 days by 2–4% if sentiment is high or volatile.
- If sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00 values), model tends to over-forecast — apply downward correction of 3–5% to peak days.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after forecast peak, model often fails to anticipate — add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast 3–5 days after peak.
